text:
Sam: Noticing a subtle perf regression on the host stack after yesterday's automatic kernel rebalancing. p95 overall ok, but p99 tail for `host_tokenize+parse` increased ~18% on canary. Any quick theories?

Priya: I pulled a couple of short traces. The extra time lives in our stream framing + syscall layer. Lots of tiny writev calls and repeated small buffer allocations.

Lee: Confirmed. Flame shows more time in `stream::flush_partial` and `http2::frame_write`. The new kernel path appears to prefer earlier emission for partial frames (latency-minded), but that backfires with more syscalls.

Anika: Holding hypothesis: kernel selector change tweaked sequence length distribution seen by the host, which reduced our batching window and increased KV cache misses (fewer shared prefixes). KV misses cause sync hang on hotpath.

Sam: Repro harness: run `scripts/loadgen --workload mixed_short_long --canary` and tail /metrics/tokenize_latency_p99. I reproduced locally.

Priya: Quick numbers from canary vs baseline after 30m:
- baseline p99 host parse: 195ms
- canary p99 host parse: 230ms
- kvcache hitrate baseline: 91% -> canary: 87%
- writev/sec baseline: 180 -> canary: 410

Lee: Oof, writev more than doubled. That explains syscall pressure. Also saw minor increase in GC on host due to more short-lived buffers.

Anika: We should check whether prefix key normalization changed. If the kernel backend changed tokenization normalization (unicode folding, trimming), keys will differ and kill locality. Suggest sampling kv keys and first 32 chars.

Sam: Good call. Add env: `KV_SAMP_RATE=0.005` and `KV_KEY_PREVIEW=32` on canary.

Priya: I'll run A/B with pinned kernel vs auto-select for 45m with extra telemetry. Will capture batch_size histogram, kv hits, writev count, allocs/sec.

Lee: Meanwhile I can push a temporary patch to the host proxy: simple coalescer that groups writes up to 4KB or up to 10ms. Low-risk feature flag. If that brings writev/sec down and p99 improves, then syscall churn is the main factor.

Anika: If coalescer helps but KV hitrate still drops, we might need both: revert kernel selector change (or adjust sequence heuristics) and keep coalescer as mitigation.

Sam: Also note: one micro-optimizer in the old kernel path compacted token emits into larger buffers before handing to the framing layer. That path was disabled by the new selector. If that's the case, re-enabling compact emit might be cheaper than proxy coalescer. Lee, can you check that?

Lee: I'll grep and diff tokenizer codepath flags across kernel variants. If we can re-enable compact emit behind a feature flag, low-risk test.

Priya: A/B results halfway: p99 pinned=198ms, p99 auto=233ms. writev/sec pinned=170, auto=420. kv hitrate pinned=90.8%, auto=86.9%. Coalescer experiment queued.

ops-bot: Canary pinned to previous kernel on 8 nodes. Reminder: manual unpause required to continue rollout.

Sam: Thanks. Next steps: (1) sample KV keys to validate normalization drift, (2) validate batch_size and batching-window changes, (3) run host-proxy coalescer experiment, (4) try re-enabling compact-token-emit under FF. We'll hold the kernel rollout until we have root cause.

Anika: I'll instrument key-sampling today and share a small csv of top key prefixes. If I see differing prefixes (>1% divergence), that's likely the cause.

Lee: Pushed coalescer flag to canary as FF=coalesce_v1. Running smoke now.

Priya: Early coalescer result (10m window): writev/sec dropped 420 -> 95 on coalescer nodes, p99 host parse improved 233 -> 210 but still above baseline. KV hitrate unchanged. That points to mixed causes: syscall churn and KV churn both contributing.

Sam: Good intermediate signal. If KV hitrate unchanged, normalization/batching causing misses independent of write pattern. Anika, share key sample when ready.

Anika: Uploaded key sample: https://internal.redwood/data/kv-samples/7023456789-keys.csv. Quick look: many keys differ at byte 12 where the tokenizer used to strip trailing spaces; new backend preserves them. Looks like normalization difference.

Lee: That would explain misses. Fix path: either align tokenizer normalization across kernels (preferred), or add normalization shim before kv keying. Shim is safer short-term.

Priya: For immediate rollback criteria: if p99 host parse >220ms for >=10min AND kv hitrate drop >=3% vs baseline, rollback kernel selector. We're currently exceeding those in canary.

ops-bot: Alert rule created: writev/sec spike OR kv_hitrate_drop >=3% => notify #eng-runtime + auto-pause canary.

Sam: Action items assigned: Anika(normalization shim + key-sample analysis), Lee(compact-emit flag + coalescer tuning), Priya(full A/B traces + perf counters). We'll reconvene after fixes. Keep updates here.

Priya: Posting full perf bundle: https://internal.redwood/perf/bundles/7023456789-ab.tar.gz

Sam: Thanks all. TL;DR: kernel auto-selection changed tokenization/emit behavior, causing more small writes and different KV key shapes; both raised p99. Holding rollout and testing two mitigations (coalescer, normalization shim).

Lee: +1.
